glossary.Mucosal: Relating to the moist lining of the mouth, genitals or eyes.
glossary.Oral herpes: HSV infection of the lips and mouth, usually seen as cold sores.
glossary.Genital herpes: HSV infection of the genitals, causing painful ulcers; usually HSV-2.
glossary.Immunosuppression: Weakened immune defences, from drugs or disease.
glossary.Intercurrent illness: Another illness happening at the same time, which can trigger reactivation.
glossary.Latent: Present but dormant, not causing symptoms.
glossary.Ulcers: Breaks in the skin or mucosa exposing the tissue underneath.
glossary.Recurrent herpes: Repeat outbreaks after the first infection, due to reactivation of latent virus.
glossary.Keratitis: Inflammation or infection of the cornea.
glossary.Corneal: Relating to the cornea, the clear front window of the eye.
glossary.Foreign body sensation: Feeling that something is stuck in the eye.
glossary.Concentric: Rings sharing the same centre, like a target.
glossary.Congenital: Present at or acquired around birth.
glossary.Neonatal: Relating to a newborn baby in the first 28 days.
glossary.Sepsis: Life-threatening organ dysfunction caused by a dysregulated response to infection.
glossary.Swab: A cotton-tipped stick rubbed on a lesion to collect a sample.
glossary.Paracetamol: A simple painkiller and fever reducer.
glossary.Topical: Applied directly to the skin or eye surface.
glossary.Topical steroids: Steroid creams or drops; in HSV keratitis they let the virus spread and worsen the ulcer.
glossary.Double-stranded DNA virus: A virus whose genome is two-stranded DNA, like all herpesviruses.
glossary.Sensory nerve ganglia: Clusters of sensory nerve cell bodies beside the brainstem or spinal cord where HSV hides.
glossary.UV exposure: Sunlight, a common trigger for cold sore reactivation.
glossary.Intraepidermal: Within the epidermis, the outer skin layer.
glossary.Blister: A bubble of fluid within or under the skin.
glossary.Olfactory: Relating to the sense of smell; the olfactory tract runs to the temporal lobe.
glossary.Trigeminal tracts: Pathways of the trigeminal nerve, which carries sensation from the face.
glossary.Antigens: Molecules the immune system recognises as foreign.
glossary.Immune complex: Antigen bound to antibody, which can deposit in tissue and cause inflammation.
glossary.Dermo-epidermal junction: Boundary between the epidermis and the dermis below it.
glossary.Genital secretions: Fluids from the genital tract, which carry virus during an outbreak.
glossary.Vaginal delivery: Birth through the birth canal, exposing the baby to genital secretions.
